title: De Pont Museum presents first major Dutch exhibition of Sigmar Polke since 1992
summary: This autumn, De Pont Museum presents Sigmar Polke – The Knowledge of Colours, the first major exhibition in the Netherlands of Sigmar Polke (Oels, 1941 – Cologne, 2010) since his retrospective at the Stedelijk Museum in 1992. Developed in collaboration with the Anna Polke Foundation, the exhibition brings together more than fifty works from the 1980s to the late 2000s, focusing on Polke’s experimental approach to colour, pigment and unconventional painting materials. Alongside ensembles from the ‘Collectie Nederland’ (the joint Dutch museum collections), brought together for the first time, the exhibition includes important loans from private and museum collections in Germany, France and the United Kingdom, among others. The works in the exhibition mark a crucial turning point in Polke’s oeuvre. Of particular importance was the journey that took him in 1980/81 to Australia, Papua New Guinea and Southeast Asia. title: The Rockwell Museum celebrates 50 years of collecting American art with 'Rockwell Reframed'
summary: For the last five decades, The Rockwell Museum , a Smithsonian Affiliate, has served as a dynamic cultural anchor in New York’s Southern Tier, connecting audiences to the evolving story of the American experience. The Museum is marking its 50th anniversary with the publication of “Rockwell Reframed: 50 Years of Collecting American Art,” available Sept 25. The book demonstrates the breadth and diversity of the institution’s holdings through 50 works, featured with fresh insights, new scholarship, and striking photography. Together, they offer a reflective look into the Museum’s history and set the stage for its future. title: The Raclin Murphy Museum of Art announces new Teaching Gallery exhibition for Fall semester 2026
summary: The Raclin Murphy Museum of Art has opened its latest Teaching Gallery exhibition, partnering with faculty across campus to integrate the Museum’s permanent collection into coursework and research. This semester, the Gallery features works of art selected by faculty members who teach classes and lead programs in theology, art history, global affairs, the Initiative on Race and Resilience, and the Moreau First-Year Seminar. By displaying works of art currently not on view, the gallery bridges academic scholarship and visual art. The diversity of works of art and classes represented make the dynamic, interdisciplinary learning at Notre Dame visible both to campus visitors and the public. “The Raclin Murphy welcomes faculty from any discipline to select works of art that support their specific course goals,” said Bridget Hoyt, curator of education for academic

title: Hake's to auction Part 1 of the legendary Lawrence Klein collection of vintage comics and original art
summary: Hake’s is gearing up to auction Part 1 of the Lawrence Klein collection, an astounding assemblage of vintage comic books and original comic book art by one of the industry’s truly legendary collectors and longtime insiders. The fully-illustrated catalog is up now on Hake’s website and bidding will open on Monday, September 28 at 9am ET. All lots will begin closing at 9:40pm on Wednesday, October 21. Lawrence Klein was bitten by the comic bug at an early age. His parents encouraged him to read as a child, and comics were a welcome presence in their home. Growing up outside New York City, Lawrence commuted into the city with his father for early comic conventions like Creation Con, meeting comic creators and getting them to sign copies of the comics they worked on. title: Erika Giovanna Klien retrospective opens at Lower Belvedere in Vienna
summary: As an outstanding representative of Viennese Kineticism, Erika Giovanna Klien (1900–1957) soon shot to international fame. Her passion for the theater and dance led to innovative stage designs and complex depictions of bodies in motion. From 1929 Klien lived in New York, which resulted in an increased focus on urban spaces and social issues. The exhibition at the Lower Belvedere shines a spotlight on every facet of the painter, graphic designer, and art educator’s oeuvre and presents the latest research on her life and work. General Director Stella Rollig: Some forty years since Erika Giovanna Klien’s first solo exhibition in a museum, this show presents a contemporary perspective on the artist and invites visitors to learn about new facets of her creative output. title: Christie's New York presents Post-War to Present
summary: Christie's announced Post-War to Present taking place live on October 1st at Christie's Rockefeller Center saleroom in New York. The sale kicks off the fall season of 20/21 sales with an enviable selection of works by a diverse cross-section of post-war and contemporary artists working across mediums of all types. In total, the sale includes 236 works and is expected to achieve more than $26.9 million. Kathryn Marber, Head of Sale, Post-War to Present, says, “This fall, Christie's Post-War to Present sale brings together a dynamic range of works spanning generations, from the pioneering figures who reshaped the course of twentieth-century art to some of the most compelling voices working today. title: David Kordansky Gallery presents Keith Sonnier light sculptures in Los Angeles
summary: David Kordansky Gallery is presenting Keith Sonnier: Inside Light, 1968–1970, the gallery’s second solo exhibition of works by Keith Sonnier (b. 1941, d. 2020), a major postwar American artist whose singular vision encompassed advances in sculpture, painting, installation, video, and performance. Inside Light, which was previously presented at David Kordansky’s New York gallery in 2024, features Sonnier’s earliest experiments with neon and argon, which mark the beginning of his career-long exploration of new technologies and materials. Throughout a career spanning six decades, Sonnier authored a complex body of work that challenges dogmas at the heart of twentieth- and twenty-first-century art historical narratives, often questioning previous conceptions of what sculpture—and indeed, art itself—could be and do. title: Memphis museum exhibits permanent collection honoring its 50-year history
summary: This fall, Dixon Gallery and Gardens presents “An Investment in Pleasure: Fifty Years of the Dixon Gallery and Gardens Collection,” celebrating the museum’s permanent collection. On view in the main galleries from Sept. 20 to Jan. 10, 2027, the exhibition features works of art from founders Margaret and Hugo Dixon and acquisitions made by the museum during its 50 years, including works purchased by the Curator’s Circle. Installing more works than ever before in its galleries, this display features more than 100 pieces in the order in which they came to the permanent collection. The Dixons spent a lifetime collecting high-quality fine-art pieces, considering each object “an investment in pleasure” – something to uplift and inspire them every day. title: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art celebrates star-studded opening in Los Angeles
summary: On Saturday, September 19, 2026, Co-Founders George Lucas and Mellody Hobson hosted Opening Night for the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, part of a series of inaugural events culminating in the public opening on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. Dedicated to the universal tradition of telling stories through images and encompassing everything from prehistoric cave paintings to today’s screen art, the Museum explores and celebrates the power of visual storytelling to inspire individuals, give shape to beliefs and ideals, and forge community. title: LACMA presents major textile retrospective for Reiko Sudō and NUNO
summary: The Los Angeles County Museum of Art presents Textile Alchemy: The Art of Reiko Sudō & NUNO. Reiko Sudō is an acclaimed Japanese designer who has pioneered innovative textiles for more than four decades. NUNO, a textile collective in Japan led by Sudō, has transformed Japanese textile design through experimentation with traditional and contemporary materials and techniques. The largest in-depth survey to date, this exhibition traces Sudō and NUNO’s innovative processes with technology and sustainability initiatives, often created in collaboration with independent artisans and workshops across Japan and utilized by celebrated architects. title: Meteorites and man-made minerals in new museum display
summary: A new permanent display, Evolving Earth, explores how the diversity of minerals has increased over time – from the formation of the first diamonds preserved in the Allende Meteorites reflecting the early universe, right up to a plastic pipe with gypsum crystals less than 40 years old. While gypsum is a naturally occurring substance, human industrial activity has had a significant impact on where and in what forms it is found. Dr Rachel Walcott, Principal Curator of Earth Systems, said: “The story of mineral formation is a central part of the story of our planet, so it’s important to bring it up to date with examples of the impact of humans on processes which have been going on almost since the universe began. As minerals and rocks continue to form, humans are leaving their imprint on the geological record, leading scientists to coin the term Anthropocene. title: Picasso and Bacon brought together in landmark comparative exhibition
summary: This major show undertakes an exciting juxtaposition of the 20th century’s two most important figurative painters: Pablo Picasso and Francis Bacon. Bacon was inspired to become a painter by Picasso’s works. Throughout his life, he would compete with him, eventually striving to surpass him. Bacon wanted to be the late 20th-century version of what Picasso was to its first half: a chronicler of being human in all of its tornness. Both of these seminal artists placed human existence at the core of their pictorial worlds. The subject they shared was the human figure – pulled apart, thrown back together, and reinvented with an unprecedented savagery. In their distorted portrayals, they elucidated pain, desire, and vulnerability, holding up a merciless mirror to the modern soul. title: Cleveland Museum of Art presents major exhibition of Andrew Wyeth watercolors
summary: Spectacular Freedom: Andrew Wyeth and the Modern American Watercolor at the Cleveland Museum of Art offers the first in-depth exploration of Andrew Wyeth’s relationship with watercolor. Featuring nearly 75 rarely seen works from the artist’s estate—including 17 that have never been on view publicly and five that have not been exhibited in nearly a century—this scholarly exhibition is groundbreaking in size and depth. Selected tempera paintings accompany the watercolors and explore the deep connection and surprising interdependency of the two mediums in Wyeth’s practice—revealing just how much of his career was spent thinking about, and working on, paper. The ticketed exhibition, on view from Sunday, September 20, 2026, through Monday, January 18, 2027, in the Kelvin and Eleanor Smith Foundation Gallery, is the first Cleveland presentation of this celebrated artist’s work. title: Ann Leda Shapiro exhibition Through the Tunnel opens at François Ghebaly
summary: François Ghebaly is presenting Through the Tunnel, an exhibition of recent works on paper by Ann Leda Shapiro, complemented by selected earlier works from an oeuvre that spans six decades. Throughout her career, Shapiro has charted the interconnected nature of our world: the way humans are both nested within a larger ecological framework, yet contain intricate networks within themselves. In the works on view in Through the Tunnel, the macrocosm mirrors the microcosm, emphasizing the cyclical nature of birth, life, and death. The title of Shapiro’s exhibition evokes anatomical nervous and vascular systems, which themselves echo root patterns of the natural world. The philosophical core of Shapiro’s work is that no one system can be isolated from all others. Through the Tunnel is anchored in Healing Scrolls, a large-

title: Collezione Olgiati presents Jannis Kounellis exhibition focusing on painting
summary: The Collezione Giancarlo e Danna Olgiati presents Jannis Kounellis: Io sono un pittore. Curated by Vincenzo de Bellis, the exhibition project takes painting, for the first time, as the principal interpretative lens through which to consider the work of Jannis Kounellis (Piraeus, 1936–Rome, 2017). It thus proposes an alternative critical perspective—broader and more radical—than the simple reception of the artist as one of the leading figures of Arte Povera, or as a master of installation and poet of matter, as he has often been celebrated. The starting point and guiding thread of the exhibition is a simple phrase, often repeated by Kounellis: “I am a painter,” not the assertion of a technique or a format, but the declaration of an attitude towards reality. “The Greek term zográfos—painter: one who “writes life”—has guided the entire curatorial project. title: South Asian Modern + Contemporary Art at Christie's totals: $22,574,720
summary: The market for South Asian Modern + Contemporary art continued to show its strength today as Christie's sale totaled $22,574,720, which was more than three times the total low estimate. All of the lots sold. Among the highlights of the sale were two important early pictures by Francis Newton Souza Woman with Lamp (1949), which made $2,304,000, almost six times its low estimate, and Building in Trafalgar Square (1955), which made $ 1,120,000. Other top results from the auction included A Progression of Sales, a sweeping 1969 landscape by Jehangir Sabavala, which made $768,000 and Ganesh Pyne's The Slave, which made $1,152,000 more than four times its low estimate. title: Louis Fratino expands thematic repertoire in new London exhibition Prose
summary: David Zwirner announces Prose, a presentation of work by Louis Fratino on view at the location in London. Prose features new paintings that expand his thematic repertoire, bringing his distinctive attention to the glorious and the everyday in both public and private life. New works elaborate on Fratino’s engagement with his immediate surroundings and the history of painting. Prose marks the New York–based artist’s first solo exhibition in London and his first with the gallery since the announcement of his representation earlier this year. Fratino creates paintings, drawings, and sculptures that depict intimate personal experiences, frequently centring contemporary queer life and the male body. title: High Museum of Art presents largest survey of Walter Wick's work
summary: Renowned worldwide for his iconic “I SPY!” and “Can You See What I See?” children’s book series, Walter Wick (American, born 1953) is one of the nation’s most famous photographic illustrators. Throughout his decades-long career, his award-winning books have captivated readers across cultures and generations, combining art, craft and technology to inspire discovery and wonder. This fall, the High Museum of Art presents “I SPY! Walter Wick’s Hidden Wonders” (Aug. 28, 2026-Jan. 3, 2027), the largest survey of Wick’s work to date, which celebrates his unique approach to storytelling through beloved images, rarely seen works and three-dimensional models. title: Whitney Museum presents Coumba Samba's first solo museum exhibition
summary: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Coumba Samba: Stars and Stripes. The exhibition marks the first solo museum presentation devoted to New York-based Senegalese American artist Coumba Samba (b. 2000), whose ambitious installations examine the social, political, and economic systems embedded within the built environment. In Stars and Stripes, Samba draws on the geometric forms and bold colors of modernist abstraction to explore the entanglement of resource extraction, militarism, and systems of global power. Sculptures modeled after depleted uranium shells are painted in the colors of the flags of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Namibia, Niger, and the United States. title: Karma presents Felipe Suzuki's first solo exhibition with the gallery
summary: Felipe Suzuki begins his compositions like a still life painter: arranging objects such as fruit on a table, paying attention to how light dapples the skin. Rather than working from observation, however, the São Paulo–based artist paints through the lens of memory, calling on the sensations and associations prompted by the initial act of looking. The resulting luminous, tranquil oil paintings register both visual and unseen worlds. “Sometimes our perspective,” he notes, “is realer than reality.” The works in this exhibition, his first solo show with Karma, were all made in 2026. Suzuki uses centuries-old painting techniques to create work that is only allusively representational. title: ICA at VCU presents trio of solo exhibitions by Tony Cokes, Cassi Namoda, and Diane Severin Nguyen
summary: The Institute for Contemporary Art at Virginia Commonwealth University presents three solo exhibitions of works by multidisciplinary artists Tony Cokes, Cassi Namoda and Diane Severin Nguyen, from September 18, 2026, to February 21, 2027, at the Markel Center. The fall exhibitions include a survey of works created over more than three decades by Richmond-born Cokes, new site-specific commissions by the internationally recognized Namoda, and a sonic installation piece by Severin Nguyen, all of whom are recognized for distinctive practices that span film, photography, painting, sculpture, installation and performance. title: Foam presents major solo exhibition of photographer Nadav Kander
summary: Foam presents The edge of things, a major solo exhibition of the internationally renowned artist Nadav Kander. Over four decades, Kander has created some of the most celebrated images in contemporary photography, including portraits of Barack Obama, Rosamund Pike and David Lynch for publications such as The New York Times Magazine, The New Yorker and TIME. Kander has exhibited widely at museums and institutions internationally, developing a body of work that moves fluidly across landscape, portraiture, still life and studies of the human form. The edge of things traces the threads that connect his work: a deep concern with the fragility of human existence, the passage of time, and the quiet intensity of everyday life. title: Hammonds House Museum opens an exhibition by Maurice Evans and Grace Kisa
summary: Hammonds House Museum is presentiing NU AFRICANS. The artworks consider the notion that Africans of the Diaspora through the circumstances of bondage and oppression have evolved into their own tribe complete with cultural practices and their own language. Maurice Evans calls them “NU AFRICANS.” Inspired by the legendary warriors and queens on the African continent, each woman was costumed by Grace Kisa and photographed by Maurice in two looks, as a warrior and a queen. The inspiration for this exhibit takes its roots from Africa, but the women featured are from this time and place. The intention of this project is to subvert existing stereotypes and prejudice, challenge the viewer to consider beauty beyond a eurocentric aesthetic, while creating space and offering agency, engaging the mechanism of Afrofuturism to imagine

title: Columbus Museum of Art presents Clare Rojas: Returning
summary: The Columbus Museum of Art presents Clare Rojas: Returning, the first major hometown exhibition of Columbus-born artist Clare Rojas. On view from September 18, 2026 through February 7, 2027, the exhibition is curated by Anna Katherine Brodbeck, Deputy Director for Curatorial Affairs, and brings together more than 70 works made over the past fifteen years. A painter, sculptor, installation artist, and musician, Rojas has built a cross-disciplinary practice that bridges abstraction, folk imagery, feminism, ecology, spirituality, music, and storytelling. Born and raised in Columbus, Rojas spent much of her career in Northern California before recently returning to Ohio.
